papers.title: Heterogeneous Task Allocation for GPU-Accelerated Graph Processing in Data-Intensive Systems
papers.abstract: Large-scale graph processing is fundamental to many modern data-intensive applications, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and knowledge graph reasoning. The increasing complexity of graph algorithms and the surge in data sizes have driven the adoption of heterogeneous computing architectures combining CPUs and GPUs. However, existing task allocation strategies often fail to fully exploit the complementary strengths of these processors due to the irregular and dynamic nature of graph workloads. This paper proposes a novel heterogeneous task allocation framework specifically designed for GPU-accelerated graph processing in data-intensive systems. The framework features a lightweight runtime profiler that characterizes workload phases, a learning-based scheduler that dynamically adapts task partitioning, and a data-aware transfer mechanism that minimizes PCIe overhead. Evaluation on large-scale real-world graphs with up to billions of edges shows that our approach achieves up to 2.8× speedup and 45% energy savings compared to state-of-the-art static partitioning methods. The framework is integrated into a popular open-source graph processing system and demonstrates robust performance across diverse graph types and algorithm variations.
